object_description: Angled group of independent school and sports hall volumes
design_condition: The buildings are precisely aligned with the adjacent industrial hall while grouping around a playground and grass field, with entrances and break areas set back from traffic and the sports hall independently connected to parking.

positive.statement: The buildings form a spacious and convincing overall complex in relation to the residential development.

position.rationale: Top view shows two angled volumes grouped around a central open access zone; elevations corroborate the compact complex.

positive.statement: The outdoor spaces have beautiful spatial relationships and high quality in use and access.

position.rationale: Open space is approximated in the visible gap between the two sampled building volumes.

positive.statement: The entrances and break areas are set back from traffic and protected.

position.rationale: Set-back access and break areas are approximated along the central front-facing gap.

positive.statement: The sports hall is functionally well connected to parking and can operate completely separately from school operations.

position.rationale: The distinct lower-right volume is treated as the sports hall, with its external connection approximated toward the east.

positive.statement: The clear building structure enables a high degree of flexibility in classroom layout and allocation.

position.rationale: Classroom organization is assigned to the larger upper-left school volume visible in the top view.

positive.statement: The central access zone with opposing cascade staircases is spatially attractive.

position.target: central access zone with cascade staircases
position.rationale: The central gap and adjacent stepped linear traces identify the access zone between the angled volumes.

positive.statement: The project has a relatively cheap building volume and below-average expected investment and management costs.

position.rationale: Cost judgment concerns the project globally and has no useful spatial referent.

positive.statement: The balanced ratio of window to wall areas is particularly noticeable in sustainability terms.

position.rationale: Facade bands are visible in elevations, but window-to-wall balance is not separately distinguishable.

negative.statement: The outdoor design is somewhat schematic in its implementation.

position.rationale: The schematic outdoor condition is assigned to the open areas separating the sampled volumes.

negative.statement: The limited distance from the eastern industrial area is expected to cause disruptions to school operations.

position.rationale: Eastern site edge is approximated beyond the rightmost building volume in the top and east views.

negative.statement: The integration of ball-stopping fences is spatially problematic and may disrupt school operations.

position.rationale: Fence locations are not distinguishable; a constrained marker is placed within the central outdoor zone.

negative.statement: The ground-floor layout, sanitary rooms and escape stairs raise structural and organizational questions.

position.target: ground-floor layout, sanitary rooms and escape stairs
position.rationale: Ground-level organizational concerns are assigned to the lower surface of the larger school volume.

negative.statement: The kindergarten cloakroom corridor appears problematic because it is illuminated only through the kindergarten rooms.

position.rationale: The corridor is approximated inside the school volume; its internal daylight path is absent from the exterior sample.

negative.statement: The auditorium and adjoining rooms would have to be optimized.

position.rationale: Adjoining-room concerns are assigned to the distinct lower-right volume as an approximate internal zone.

negative.statement: The sanitary rooms are confusingly arranged and far too small.

position.rationale: Sanitary rooms are not visible internally; the marker is constrained within the larger school volume.

negative.statement: The sports hall adjoining rooms require more operationally balanced allocation across the floors.

position.rationale: The distinct sports-hall volume anchors an approximate upper adjoining-room allocation.

negative.statement: The facades remain schematic and lack the public character of a school and sports facility.

position.rationale: Elevation views directly show the long, repetitive facade bands of the sampled volumes.

negative.statement: The materialization should be differentiated more carefully inside and outside to support the atmosphere of a primary school building.

position.rationale: Material differentiation is unobservable internally; the marker uses the larger school mass as a surface proxy.

negative.statement: The widely projecting upper floors are complex and contradict the more vertical structure.

position.rationale: Upper projecting bands are visibly distinct in the top and elevation views, especially on the lower-right volume.

negative.statement: The fire-protection solutions should be questioned regarding the effort involved.

position.rationale: Fire-protection systems are not represented distinctly; a constrained marker uses the school building surface.
